doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Hearing John Coltrane's quartet in Indianapolis and being changed by it
summary: On a night off in Indianapolis she heard Coltrane with McCoy Tyner, Jimmy Garrison and Elvin Jones, and the next night found herself playing things she had never played.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: I went to hear Coltrane. It changed my life. Jimmy and I played together in Indianapolis. The club was the Embers. That was called the Embers. Down the street in another club, Coltrane was playing. He was playing on our night off, so we went, and it was the original group. It was McCoy [Tyner], Jimmy Garrison, Elvin [Jones], and Monk.

I mean Trane. I’m sorry. I’m losing my mind. It was just . . . I think he spent the whole set maybe playing two tunes or one tune or something, but it was so exciting and absorbing. I couldn’t move. It was . . . I don’t know what to say except that it was very . . .

Intense. Moving and exciting. But it’s funny, because it did affect me musically. The next night on the gig I found myself playing stuff I’d never played before. Everybody remarked on it. “What are you doing? I never heard you do that before.” It gave me a jumping off point to improve my playing.
